notes.1: This was answered correctly by most candidates.
notes.3: Candidates found this question one of the most challenging on the paper. It appeared that many candidates thought that because the ball is still falling with an increasing velocity then there must be an increasing acceleration.
notes.5: Although there were many candidates who answered correctly, option B was often chosen with these candidates knowing that this is a true statement (even though it does not explain why all objects fall with the same acceleration) without checking the remaining options carefully.
notes.8: The question was answered correctly by the majority of candidates, but some simply added the two forces as though they were acting in the same direction.
notes.11: The majority of candidates answered correctly but a significant minority made the error of thinking that the CFL lamp gave out the most light energy. To show which lamp gives out the most energy a simple calculation needed to be done (10% of 150 W = 15 W; 30% of 40 W = 12 W).
notes.13: Nearly equal numbers of candidates thought that the distance from the bottom of the barometer tube and from the reservoir surface, to the mercury level in the tube was the required distance.
notes.21: This was answered correctly by many candidates but a significant number gave the wrong option.
notes.24: This question was only answered correctly by stronger candidates. Common errors were failing to convert kilometres to metres and not allowing for the time for the light to travel both to and from the moon.
notes.27: Many candidates were unclear about the nature of ultrasound. More candidates selected option D than the key, B .
notes.33: This question proved challenging for many candidates.
notes.34: This question was answered quite well, showing a good understanding of potential dividers.
notes.36: Stronger candidates were able to recognise the application of the concept that an induced e.m.f. tends to oppose the change causing it.
notes.key_messages: Many candidates were able to show a thorough knowledge of the basic facts and relationships between quantities and had a good understanding of a range of concepts.
notes.general_comments: Candidates answered Questions 1 , 4 , 7 , 15 , 20 , 26 , 30 , 37 and 39 well, but found Questions 3 , 24 , 27, 33 and 36 more challenging.
